Testimony of Sen. Cameron Reny introducing
LD 1319, "An Act to Amend the Law Regarding the Suspension of Licenses
Issued by the Department of Marine Resources for Failure to Comply with
Reporting Requirements"
before the Joint Standing Committee on Marine Resources April 17, 2025
Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and honorable colleagues on the Joint Standing Committee on
Marine Resources, I am Senator Cameron Reny, and I represent District 13, which includes most of Lincoln County and the towns of Washington and Windsor. Today, I am presenting LD 1319, "An Act to Amend the Law Regarding the Suspension of Licenses Issued by the Department of Marine
Resources for Failure to Comply with Reporting Requirements."
This bill from the Department of Marine Resources would allow the Department to suspend a license during the fishing season for failure to submit daily harvest reports. These reports are currently required for the herring and menhaden fisheries, which are subject to quotas that must be monitored in real time.
As it stands now, the Department has no license suspension process for daily reporting, so it can only compel compliance when licenses come up for renewal each spring. This is ofien too late if quotas
have been exceeded.
To put it simply ----- the Department cannot monitor quotas in real-time and prevent fishing over quote
without daily reports. LD 1319 would create a process to suspend a license for failing to provide daily
reports. The suspension would be lifted immediately upon the provision of the missing reports. Once in compliance, license holders can go right back to fishing.
There will be testimony from the Department and others coming behind me, and I ask that you direct
ftuther technical questions to them.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,

Cameron Reny
State Senator, District 13
Representing Lincoln County and the towns of Washington and Windsor

190608:
TESTIMONY OF
Deirdre Gilbert
Department of Marine Resources
The Department of Marine Resources (DMR) is testifying
In Support of
LD 1319 An Act to Amend the Law Regarding the Suspension of Licenses issued by the Department of
Marine Resources for Failure to Comply with Reporting Requirements Before the Committee on Marine Resources Sponsored by Senator Reny Date of Hearing: April 17, 2025
Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members ofthe Joint Standing Committee on Marine
Resources, my name is Deirdre Gilbert, Director of State Marine Policy for DMR and I am testifying on
behalf of the Department in support of LD 1319. This is a Department bill, and we are grateful to
Senator Reny for sponsoring this bill on our behalf.
Under existing law, a marine resources license holder may be suspended for failure to comply with either weekly or monthly reporting requirements. This suspension authority was created in 2013. At
that time, there were no fisheries that had daily harvester reporting requirements, so a process to suspend for failure to meet daily harvester reporting requirements was not created.
Since that time, and with the advent of electronic reporting technology, daily harvester reporting
requirements have been established for both the herring and menhaden fisheries. This was necessary because both of these fisheries are subject to quotas that must be monitored in real time. The fishery is closed when the quota is reached.
Daily electronic harvester reporting has been required in the menhaden fishery for over 5 years. While
compliance has improved over time, having complete reports remains a challenge in a fishery of nearly
400 license holders. However, because there is no suspension process for daily reporting the only way for the Department to compel the submission of missing reports is when the license holder attempts to renew their license the following spring, at which point the renewal can be withheld until the reports
are provided. In 2023, at the time of license renewal DMR received reports of nearly 1 million pounds
of menhaden landings that were not submitted during the season. This caused Maine to exceed its
quota, which then had to be paid back in the 2024 season.
With this proposed change in law, DMR could suspend a license during the fishing season for failure to
submit daily reports. We do not anticipate implementing these suspensions following a single missing
report, but at key times in the fishery, such as once the state allocated quota has been reached, and prior to entering the Episodic Event Set Aside. LD 1319 spells out a process consistent with that of the processes for weekly and monthly reporting shortcomings. Like the existing landings suspensions, the suspension for failing to provide daily reports is lifted immediately upon the provision of the missing
reports. We anticipate that this will improve our ability to obtain reports in season and avoid
overages.

Following review of this bill by DM R's Assistant Attorney General, it was recommended that the
language regarding the daily reports be amended to specify that it is those reports that were
"established by rule pursuant to section 6173" , for consistency with the other sections.
Thank you for your consideration and I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.
10044897:
Matt Gilley Harpswell LD 1319
Good afternoon Good afternoon senator Tepler and Representative Hepler and members of the marine resource committee. My name is Matt Gilley and I am a zone F council representative and a Cundys harbor lobster boat captain. I'm writing to you today in extremely strong opposition to ld 1319 An Act to Amend the Law Regarding the Suspension of Licenses Issued by the Department of Marine Resources for Failure to Comply with Reporting Requirements. Reporting for lobster harvesting began a couple of years ago at the state level and became a federal requirement last year. Upon implementation last year by the federal government there were numerous problems with the application we had to use to report. I can only speak for myself I filed 122 reports last year. I had issues on 48 different occasions. I spent countless weeks on the phone with DMR trying to work through the problems. They were always extremely helpful. Most of the issues I had came from issues with the application we were using or a problem or at the federal level with the server. None of my issues were caused by myself and the state can attest to this. Most recently in March when I went to renew my federal permit I was found out of compliance. Upon investigation I was told I was missing over 300 reports over the last couple years. I had purchased my federal permit several years prior and the system wanted me to file my reports (which had already been filed once) as well as the reports for the person I had purchased my permit from. It took several weeks to solve this issue. I have had issues with even connecting to the server to submit the reports. Over 100 of the reports I submitted I had to do multiple times because of server errors. I still have errors on every report due to exporting data issues. Well over a third of the time I have tried to submit reports I have had issues that I have had to call the state spend hours of my own time in order to remain in compliance. During this time I have been unable to renew licenses and spent countless hours working through the issues on my own losing time fishing and with family. This has cost me significant financial, emotional, and mental anguish. I have expressed my dissatisfaction each time with NOAA and DMR yet the problems have continued to happen. There were multiple times I was unable to report in the 24 hour time frame because of an error on the governments end. DMR has acknowledged their frustrations with the Feds inability to fix the issues. To now move to suspend a harvesters license when they haven't reported in 24 hours is unacceptable. Will people lose their jobs if the server or application doesn't work for 24 hours? If we can't file a report because of a problem on their end why are we the only ones being penalized? I barely have the time to spend on the phone with DMR and to now have to request a hearing to keep my license is not realistic. I would have had to have had 37 hearings last year based on the way the law is written. To attempt to penalize harvesters for not complying with something that isn't compilable with in the first place just seems like a way to eliminate licenses. How about fixing the system we have to use before threatening to take our livelihoods. We've only been asking this since its inception. I urge you to vote ought not to pass on this very troublesome bill.
